uncited: The method operates during the prefix shifting phase of multi-view path tracing.
It evaluates the similarity between the scattering distribution of a candidate shifted prefix and the base prefix using a discrete approximation of the Total Variation (TV) distance.
If the distributions are sufficiently similar, the prefix is accepted; otherwise, it is rejected.
*   Scattering distribution $p$ associated with the base prefix at the pivot interaction.
*   Scattering distribution $q$ associated with the candidate prefix at the pivot interaction.
*   If accepted, a direction is sampled from the uniform mixture of accepted scattering distributions to continue the suffix.
No specific complex data structures are required beyond standard path storage.

The method requires storing the scattering function parameters (e.g., roughness, anisotropy, layer properties) at the pivot point for both the base and candidate prefixes to evaluate the PDFs $p(\omega)$ and $q(\omega)$.
**Select Evaluation Directions:** Determine a small set of directions $\{\omega_k\}_k$ to evaluate the scattering distributions.
**Stochastic Acceptance:** Compute the acceptance probability $P_{i \rightarrow j}$ based on the TV distance.
**Suffix Sampling (if accepted):** If the prefix is accepted, sample a direction $\omega$ from the uniform mixture of the scattering distributions of all accepted prefixes.
*   $p(\omega_i)$ is the PDF value of the base scattering distribution at direction $\omega_i$.
*   $q(\omega_i)$ is the PDF value of the candidate scattering distribution at direction $\omega_i$.
*   **Memory Complexity:** No additional memory overhead beyond storing the scattering function parameters at the pivot point.
